ux.adopt.title: Deployment & integration
ux.adopt.desc: Add the dependency to a Spring Boot application and mark the endpoints to protect. Start in shadow mode, which only records decisions, check the operational metrics, then switch to enforce mode.
ux.adopt.step.1.title: Add the dependency
ux.adopt.step.1.body: Add the one Spring Boot starter as a dependency.
ux.adopt.step.2.title: Mark the endpoints to protect
ux.adopt.step.2.body: Put `@EnableAISecurity` on the application and `@Protectable` on the endpoints that need a decision. `sync = true` holds the response until the decision is made (synchronous decision); the default `false` applies it from the next request (asynchronous decision).
ux.adopt.step.3.title: Start in shadow mode
ux.adopt.step.3.body: Decisions are recorded, not applied. Check the decision mix and the latency in Operational metrics, then change it to `ENFORCE`.

ux.tour.video.console.title: How to read the live decision screen
ux.tour.video.agent.title: How to hand work to a business agent
ux.tour.scene.console.request: Check the request that will go out, pick the expected decision, then send it. It can be sent once an expectation is picked.
ux.tour.scene.console.arrive: The same request reaches the five security controls at once: the web application firewall, identity & access, threshold rules, approval policy rules and Contexa.
ux.tour.scene.console.hold: Contexa holds the response while it decides; nothing leaves meanwhile. On the right, the facts checked against the behavioral baseline and the business context light up one by one.
ux.tour.scene.console.bars: Each bar is what a control actually handed over: a red bar leaked, and an empty bar means nothing left.
ux.tour.scene.console.log: The log below keeps each step with its real time since the request arrived.
ux.tour.scene.console.judgment: Contexa's decision is allow, step-up authentication, hold for review or block. This run's result shows only once it is sent.
ux.tour.scene.agent.work: The work an employee delegated to the business agent is recorded as its objective, delegated scope and delegation period; these come first.
ux.tour.scene.agent.send: The agent reads the employee's instruction and decides its requests itself. The expected decision is picked, then the work is handed to the agent.
ux.tour.scene.agent.rows: Each request the agent sent gets one row of results from the five security controls: the web application firewall, identity & access, threshold rules, approval policy rules and Contexa.
ux.tour.scene.agent.reason: The next screen sets the delegated scope, the request sent and the difference the engine named side by side, from its cited facts only.
ux.tour.scene.agent.answer: When Contexa asks for a delegator check, it is approved or rejected as the delegator. This run's result shows only once it is sent.

ux.intro.title: Contexa live demo
ux.intro.tagline: Every request that passes sign-in, decided again by its context
ux.intro.lead: Contexa is an AI decision engine that decides each request after sign-in by the behavioral baseline and the business context. This demo sends threat scenarios to the real engine and shows the results and their grounds as they are.
ux.intro.value.label: Same request, different decision
ux.intro.value.caption: The real result of the published recorded run {{run}} (scenario {{case}}). Account and permission were valid and the time and count within the rules, so the four existing controls all allowed it. Contexa's decision is {{verdict}}, weighing the behavioral baseline and the business context.
ux.intro.value.captionPlain: The five security controls receive the same request at once. A rule sees its preset conditions only; Contexa also weighs the behavioral baseline and the business context.
ux.intro.pillar.run.title: Run
ux.intro.pillar.run.body: Send account takeover, insider threat and AI agent delegation abuse scenarios to the real decision engine.
ux.intro.pillar.see.title: See
ux.intro.pillar.see.body: See the five security controls' answers to the same request beside the grounds of Contexa's decision.
ux.intro.pillar.mean.title: Meaning
ux.intro.pillar.mean.body: Threats after sign-in that rules cannot see are decided by context. The results are published as standard benchmarks and scenario validation.
